intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover to maximize your viewing experience, often venturing to remote lava fields or frozen lakes for a dramatic backdrop.
experiences.location: Þingvellir National Park, Golden Circle region

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. The average water temperature of 39°C (102°F) is perfect for relaxing while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Includes access to steam rooms, saunas, and the famous silica mud mask stations. Book well in advance as slots fill up fast.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geothermal activity, bubbling hot springs, and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this offers an authentic and intimate geothermal bathing experience in a stunning rural setting.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its culinary scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional dishes like skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, the colorful old harbor, and learn about Norse mythology and the settlement history at the Settlement Exhibition.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's otherworldly rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands to reach the legendary natural geothermal hot spring pool at Landmannalaugar. The hike winds through obsidian lava fields, steaming fumaroles, and vibrant multi-colored hills before rewarding you with a warm soak in the natural pool. A truly bucket-list Icelandic experience combining hiking and hot springs.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and baggage claim, then take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (approx 3,000 ISK) to Reykjavik area and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick snack from the airport kiosk or a vending machine upon arrival - Noodle Cup or packaged sandwich (~500-800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival night simple. Download the Aurora Forecast app (Vedur.is) to track northern lights activity during your stay. Exchange some currency or use ATM at the airport. January temperatures average -1°C to 3°C, so layer up before exiting the terminal.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a late breakfast, take a walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to acclimate to Iceland's winter landscape. Enjoy the dramatic coastal scenery and black sand shoreline - completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest geothermal hot pot or natural hot spring in the area. Many municipalities in Iceland have free or very low-cost public swimming pools with hot tubs (around 1,000-1,200 ISK). Soak and relax while chatting with locals - a quintessential Icelandic experience.
day_by_day.evening: Check the aurora forecast (scale 3+ is good). If activity is predicted, bundle up and head to a dark spot near the resort away from light pollution to watch the northern lights. Bring a tripod if you have one for photos.

meals.breakfast: Grocery store run - pick up bread, eggs, yogurt, and skyr (Icelandic yogurt) from Bonus or Kronan supermarket (~1,500 ISK for supplies). Cook in hostel-style kitchen if available at resort.
meals.lunch: Homemade sandwich with Icelandic cheese and cucumber from grocery supplies (~300 ISK)
meals.dinner: Noodles or a simple pasta dish cooked at the resort, or try a local bakery (bakarí) for a soup and bread combo (~1,200-1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January has only 5-6 hours of daylight (roughly 11am-4pm), so plan outdoor sightseeing within that window. Northern lights are best viewed after 9pm on clear nights. Aurora season is peak in January - excellent chances!

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget bus or organized day tour toward the Golden Circle - one of Iceland's most iconic routes. Start with Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Entry to the park is free; only parking costs (~750 ISK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir geothermal area to watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes shooting water 20-30 meters high. Completely free to view. Then visit Gullfoss waterfall - one of Iceland's most powerful and beautiful waterfalls, also free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon/early evening. Monitor aurora forecast - if Kp index is 3 or higher and skies are clear, head out for northern lights viewing from the beach. The coastal location provides dark skies and great horizons.

meals.breakfast: Skyr with granola and coffee prepared at the resort (~200 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade lunch - thermos of soup and sandwiches to eat at Geysir or Gullfoss picnic area (~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Stop at a local gas station (N1 or Orkan) for a budget hot dog - the famous Icelandic pylsa with all toppings (~500 ISK). These are an Icelandic institution!

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle is approximately 300km round trip. Consider renting a car with other travelers to split costs, or book a budget group day tour (~8,000-10,000 ISK per person). Roads in January can be icy - always check road.is before driving. Wear microspike shoe attachments for icy paths.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavik city center on foot. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church (exterior free, tower entry ~1,000 ISK), stroll down Laugavegur shopping street, and admire the Harpa Concert Hall architecture from outside. The colorful old harbor area is also worth a walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Árbær Open Air Museum (check if open in January - some seasonal closures) or explore the Settlement Exhibition museum (~2,200 ISK) which showcases Viking-age artifacts discovered beneath the city. Walk along the Tjörnin pond to see birds and city reflections.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights hunt from Grótta lighthouse on Seltjarnarnes peninsula - a popular and free aurora-watching spot just 15 minutes from central Reykjavik with minimal light pollution. Check forecast first.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavik Roasters or similar local café for coffee and a pastry (~1,200 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur - the most famous hot dog stand in Iceland, beloved by locals and presidents alike (~500-700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Bonus supermarket haul - cook a hearty lamb soup (kjötsúpa) using Icelandic lamb and root vegetables at the resort (~1,000 ISK for ingredients serving 2)

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavik is very walkable. Bus system (Strætó) is affordable at ~490 ISK per ride or get a day pass. Download the Strætó app for routes and real-time schedules. Many museums offer free entry on specific days - check local listings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local geothermal public swimming pool - Laugardalslaug in Reykjavik is one of the largest and most popular (entry ~1,200 ISK). Soak in the hot pots, try the steam room, and experience how Icelanders truly relax. This is a must-do cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Elliðaárdalur valley, a free nature area within Reykjavik city limits. Walk along the river where Atlantic salmon run in summer (frozen or flowing in January). Visit the nearby Árbær neighborhood for a glimpse of traditional Icelandic turf houses.
day_by_day.evening: Aurora watching session - drive or take a short bus ride outside the city to reduce light pollution. Mosfellsbær area or Heiðmörk nature reserve are good free options. Bring hot chocolate in a thermos, warm blankets, and patience.

meals.breakfast: Homemade oatmeal with dried fruit and honey at resort (~200 ISK)
meals.lunch: Grocery store deli counter - pick up Icelandic flatbread (flatbrauð) with smoked lamb (~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hlöllabátar (Subway-style Icelandic sandwich shop) for a budget-friendly baguette meal (~1,500-1,800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The public pool culture in Iceland is deeply social - it is considered rude not to shower thoroughly without a swimsuit before entering. Follow posted instructions. Bring flip flops and a towel (or rent one for ~500 ISK). January is one of the best months for northern lights due to long dark nights.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (about 2-hour drive from Reykjavik). Visit Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano, made famous by Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Walk along the Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach - free and dramatic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Arnarstapi and Hellnar coastal villages with their stunning lava arch formations and bird cliffs. Walk the free coastal trail between the two villages (about 2.5km) for spectacular ocean and glacier views. Visit Vatnshellir lava cave if budget allows (~3,500 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort. The Snæfellsnes area offers excellent northern lights viewing due to remote, dark skies. If aurora forecast is good, stop along the roadside away from any light sources for viewing before returning.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast to eat in the car - thermos of coffee, granola bars, and fruit (~300 ISK)
meals.lunch: Picnic at Djúpalónssandur beach - packed sandwiches and hot soup in thermos (~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Fjöruhúsið café in Hellnar for traditional Icelandic fish soup if budget allows (~2,500 ISK), or cook at resort upon return

day_by_day.notes: Car rental is strongly recommended for Snæfellsnes - budget around 8,000-12,000 ISK/day for a small car. Share costs with fellow travelers. Check road.is before departing - mountain roads can close in winter storms. Snæfellsnes is one of Iceland's most magical and underrated regions.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in, do laundry, restock groceries at Bonus supermarket (Iceland's cheapest chain - look for the yellow pig logo). Plan the second week of the trip and check weather forecasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local geothermal area - Reykjadalur (Steam Valley) hot spring river if accessible in winter conditions. The hike is about 3km each way and leads to a natural hot river where you can bathe for free. Check trail conditions as it can be icy in January.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights viewing from the beachfront near the resort. Set an alarm for 11pm-2am when aurora activity is typically strongest. Use the Vedur.is app for real-time cloud cover maps and aurora forecasts.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic-style breakfast at resort - eggs, skyr, bread, and coffee (~300 ISK using grocery supplies)
meals.lunch: Bonus supermarket ready-made soup or salad bar (~700-900 ISK)
meals.dinner: Cook Icelandic lamb chops or fish (cod or haddock) purchased from the supermarket - Iceland's seafood is incredibly fresh and affordable (~1,200-1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important for a 13-day journey. Reykjadalur hike in January requires crampons/microspikes and hiking poles. The reward is soaking in a naturally heated river surrounded by steaming landscape - absolutely magical and completely free. Bring a changing robe or towel.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula - a raw, volcanic landscape just 30 minutes from Keflavik airport. Visit the Bridge Between Continents (free) where you can walk between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates on a small footbridge over a fissure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Gunnuhver hot spring area on Reykjanes - a free geothermal field with massive steam vents, bubbling mud pots, and sulfuric fumaroles. The landscape looks truly otherworldly. Also visit Reykjanesviti, Iceland's oldest lighthouse, with dramatic coastal views.
day_by_day.evening: The Reykjanes Peninsula has very dark skies. If aurora forecast is favorable, this peninsula is an excellent viewing location. Drive to a high point away from roads for panoramic northern lights viewing.

meals.breakfast: Skyr parfait with berries prepared at resort (~250 ISK)
meals.lunch: Gas station lunch at N1 in Keflavik - hot dog, coffee, and a pastry (~900 ISK)
meals.dinner: Keflavik town has a few budget restaurants - try Duus Húsið for fish and chips (~2,000-2,500 ISK) or cook at resort

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is geologically one of the most active areas in Iceland. Since 2021, it has experienced multiple volcanic eruptions. Always check safety.is and vedur.is for current volcanic activity and no-go zones before visiting. The area is generally safe for tourists but stay on marked paths.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day tour or self-drive to the South Coast of Iceland. Start at Seljalandsfoss waterfall where you can walk behind the curtain of water (entry free, parking ~750 ISK). Nearby Gljúfrabúi hidden waterfall is also free and magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss waterfall - one of Iceland's biggest and most dramatic. Climb the 527 steps to the top for panoramic views (free). Then drive to Reynisfjara black sand beach near Vík - famous for its basalt column caves and sea stacks. Warning: sneaker waves are dangerous, stay back from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back along the south coast. Stop at Dyrhólaey peninsula for a free viewpoint over the black beach and sea arch. Return to resort in the evening, watch for aurora activity on the drive back through rural areas.

meals.breakfast: Pack a road trip breakfast - thermos of coffee, boiled eggs, and fruit (~300 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack lunch to eat at Skógafoss - sandwiches and hot soup in thermos (~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Vík has a few options - Suður-Vík restaurant for budget soup and bread (~1,800 ISK) or pick up supplies and cook at resort

day_by_day.notes: South Coast is approximately 180-250km from Reykjavik depending on how far you go. Roads are generally well-maintained but can be icy. Reynisfjara beach has claimed lives due to sneaker waves - never turn your back on the ocean and stay well above the waterline. The basalt columns at Reynisfjara are among the most photogenic in Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þórsmörk (Thorsmork) valley if road conditions permit (F-roads may be closed in January - check road.is). Alternatively, explore the Hveragerði geothermal town, known as the 'flower town' with greenhouses heated by geothermal energy. Walk through town and see steaming vents in people's gardens - free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hveragerði has a natural hot spring pool called Hveragerðislaug (free or small fee). Soak in geothermally heated outdoor pools surrounded by steam. Visit the local geothermal park in the town center. Browse the greenhouse tomatoes and cucumbers grown with geothermal heat.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights viewing from Hveragerði area or return to resort. The area east of Reykjavik has good aurora viewing opportunities. Set up on a hillside overlooking the valley for a dramatic backdrop if lights appear.

meals.breakfast: Homemade pancakes at resort using simple ingredients (~300 ISK)
meals.lunch: Varma café in Hveragerði for affordable soup and sandwiches (~1,200-1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Cook at resort - try making plokkfiskur (Icelandic fish stew with potatoes and béchamel) using fresh cod from supermarket (~1,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Hveragerði is only 45 minutes from Reykjavik by bus (Strætó bus 51) making it very accessible without a car. The town experienced a significant earthquake in 2008 and some geothermal vents opened directly in the streets - locals have embraced them as attractions. The hot spring hike to Reykjadalur starts from this town.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning for personal exploration near the resort. Walk along the beachfront, photograph the winter landscape and crashing waves. Look for seabirds like northern gannets, eider ducks, and if lucky, harlequin ducks along the shore. Birdwatching is free and rewarding in Iceland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local swimming pool for a long relaxing soak - try a different pool than earlier in the trip for variety. Many Icelandic towns have their own geothermal pools with unique hot pots, steam rooms, and cold plunge pools. Budget around 1,000-1,200 ISK for entry.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated northern lights hunting evening. Research the best dark sky locations near the resort, check the aurora forecast at 6pm and 9pm, and if Kp index is 2+ with clear skies, head out. Dress in maximum layers - temperatures feel much colder when standing still in the dark.

meals.breakfast: Icelandic-style breakfast - rye bread (rúgbrauð) with butter and smoked salmon (~400 ISK from supermarket)
meals.lunch: Homemade vegetable soup using root vegetables - hearty and warming (~500 ISK for ingredients)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner - Icelandic fish and chips from a local restaurant (~2,500-3,000 ISK) as a mid-trip splurge

day_by_day.notes: Day 11 is a good day to sort photos, back up memory cards, write a travel journal, or connect with family back home. Check your budget status and adjust remaining days accordingly. January 25th has approximately 6 hours of daylight. Aurora activity has been increasing - statistically, you should have seen lights by now if skies have been clear.

day_by_day.morning: Final major excursion - visit the Blue Lagoon area (the famous geothermal spa). Note: Blue Lagoon itself is expensive (~8,000-15,000 ISK). Instead, visit the nearby Grindavík town and the Sýlingarfoss waterfall area for free. Alternatively, book the budget Blue Lagoon Comfort entry well in advance if it fits your budget.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the lava fields surrounding Grindavík - walk among dramatic volcanic formations that look like a moonscape. Visit the Saltfish Museum in Grindavík (small fee) to learn about Iceland's most important historical industry. The harbor area is free to walk and interesting.
day_by_day.evening: Final dedicated aurora hunt of the trip. Return to the best dark sky spot you've found during your stay. Spend 2-3 hours watching the sky with hot drinks and warm blankets. If you haven't seen the northern lights yet, tonight is your last best chance - consider staying out until midnight.

meals.breakfast: Special last full-day breakfast - make a big spread at the resort with all remaining groceries (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Grindavík harbor café for fresh fish soup - a local specialty in this fishing town (~1,500-1,800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Cook a celebratory final dinner at the resort - lamb stew with Icelandic herbs and potatoes (~1,500 ISK for quality ingredients)

day_by_day.notes: Check the volcanic activity situation in Grindavík before visiting - the town has been affected by eruptions since 2023. Always verify safety.is for current conditions. Pack your bags tonight to make tomorrow morning smoother. Set multiple alarms for the morning. Do a final check of the resort room for forgotten items.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort and take one last walk along the beachfront. Breathe in the fresh Arctic air and reflect on your Icelandic adventure. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and load luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, use remaining hours wisely. If time allows, stop at a final geothermal pool for one last soak. Visit a local souvenir shop for budget-friendly gifts - Icelandic wool products, lava salt, and skyr chocolate are popular. Bonus supermarket has affordable Icelandic souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Keflavik International Airport. Allow at least 2-3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and customs. Enjoy a final Icelandic hot dog at the airport kiosk. Reflect on 13 incredible days of hot springs, volcanic landscapes, and hopefully, the dancing northern lights.

meals.breakfast: Use up remaining groceries for a final resort breakfast - eggs, toast, skyr, and coffee (~200 ISK)
meals.lunch: Airport or final café stop - soup and sandwich (~1,500-2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary for the trip: Accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort is your main fixed cost. Daily food budget should average 3,000-4,000 ISK/day by cooking most meals. Activities budget 2,000-5,000 ISK/day depending on tours. Transportation 1,000-3,000 ISK/day. Total estimated daily budget: 8,000-15,000 ISK (~$55-100 USD). Iceland is expensive but manageable with smart planning - cooking your own meals and choosing free natural attractions over expensive tourist traps makes a huge difference.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked transfer or rental car to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind, and get acquainted with the resort facilities. Keep an eye on the sky during the drive — January nights in Iceland offer excellent chances of spotting the northern lights on clear nights.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight)
meals.lunch: N/A (in-flight)
meals.dinner: Light snack from airport kiosk or vending machine at resort upon arrival — Keflavik Airport has a 24-hour convenience shop for essentials.

day_by_day.notes: January sunset is around 16:30 in Iceland. Arrival is well into darkness — ideal aurora-watching conditions if skies are clear. Download the Icelandic Met Office app (vedur.is) and Aurora Forecast app before landing. Dress in warm layers immediately upon exiting the terminal; temperatures can be -5°C to +4°C in January.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. Explore the beachfront area near Aegean Bliss Resort — take a brisk morning walk along the Icelandic coastline, watching for dramatic winter waves and seabirds. Familiarize yourself with the local surroundings and pick up any supplies from a nearby grocery store (Bónus or Krónan are budget-friendly Icelandic chains).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal pool rich in silica and minerals. Pre-book your entry ticket online in advance (Comfort package recommended for mid-range budget, ~8,000-9,500 ISK). Spend 2-3 hours soaking, using the silica mud mask, and enjoying the steaming lagoon. The Blue Lagoon is approximately 20-30 minutes from most beachfront areas near Keflavik.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Head to a nearby restaurant for dinner. Check aurora forecast for the night — if KP index is favorable and skies are clear, take a short drive away from any light sources near the resort for a spontaneous northern lights viewing session from the beach.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — enjoy skyr (Icelandic yogurt), fresh bread, eggs, and Icelandic dairy products.
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant or the LAVA Bar for a mid-range soup and sandwich — budget ~3,000-4,500 ISK per person.
meals.dinner: Bryggjan Brugghús or a local grill restaurant near the resort area — try lamb soup (kjötsúpa) or pan-fried Arctic char. Budget ~4,000-6,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Blue Lagoon tickets at least 2-3 weeks in advance as January is still a popular period. Remove all jewelry before entering as the silica water can damage metals. The Blue Lagoon provides robes and towels with Comfort entry.

day_by_day.morning: Drive into Reykjavik (approximately 40-50 minutes from the Keflavik area). Begin the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour — explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its culinary scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional Icelandic foods including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr, lamb dishes, and fresh seafood. Visit key landmarks like Hallgrímskirkja Church and the Sun Voyager sculpture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Reykjavik independently after the tour. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) to learn about Iceland's Viking history and culture (~2,000 ISK entry). Stroll down Laugavegur, Reykjavik's main shopping street, browsing Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), local crafts, and design shops. Pick up any souvenirs or warm gear needed for the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in downtown Reykjavik before driving back to the resort. Check aurora forecast — if conditions are excellent (KP 3+, clear skies), consider stopping at a dark spot along the drive back toward the resort for northern lights viewing.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a stop at Sandholt Bakery in Reykjavik for fresh pastries and coffee (~1,500-2,000 ISK) — one of Iceland's best artisan bakeries.
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Food & Culture Walking Tour, or supplement with a bowl of lamb soup at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja (~2,500-3,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Messinn Restaurant in Reykjavik — known for excellent skillet-served fish dishes at mid-range prices (~4,500-6,500 ISK per person). Alternatively, Sægreifinn (Sea Baron) for lobster soup (~2,500 ISK) — a beloved local institution.

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour typically runs 3-4 hours. Book in advance. Wear very warm, waterproof footwear as Reykjavik streets can be icy in January. Parking in Reykjavik is metered — use the EasyPark app.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — join a guided super jeep tour departing from the Reykjavik/Keflavik area. Expert guides use real-time weather and aurora forecasts to chase clear skies away from light pollution. Super jeeps can access remote highland tracks inaccessible to standard vehicles, maximizing your chances of seeing the aurora borealis. Tours typically depart around 21:00-22:00, so use the morning to rest and prepare. Enjoy a slow morning at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula — the volcanic landscape surrounding the resort area. Visit the Reykjanes Lighthouse (Valahnúkamöl) and the dramatic coastline with basalt rock formations. Stop at the Bridge Between Continents (Miðlína) — a footbridge spanning the rift between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates (~500 ISK fee). Visit Gunnuhver Hot Springs — a powerful geothermal area with boiling mud pools and steam vents (free entry, stay on marked paths).
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for dinner and a short rest before the Northern Lights Super Jeep tour departs (typically 21:00-22:00). Bundle up in your warmest layers — the tour lasts 3-4 hours in open wilderness. The guides will find the best location based on real-time cloud cover data.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fuel up with hearty Icelandic oatmeal, skyr, and eggs.
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch from the resort or stop at a petrol station (N1 or Orkan) for a hot dog — the Icelandic hot dog (pylsur) is a national institution at ~500-700 ISK.
meals.dinner: Early dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby casual eatery — fish and chips or lamb burger to fuel up before the evening tour. Budget ~3,500-5,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The Northern Lights Super Jeep tour is weather-dependent. Most reputable companies offer a free rebooking if the tour is cancelled due to poor conditions. Wear thermal base layers, fleece mid-layer, and a waterproof outer shell. Hand warmers are highly recommended. Bring a camera with manual settings for aurora photography.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the late-night aurora tour. Sleep in, enjoy a late resort breakfast. If the northern lights were spotted last night, review and edit your photos. Check aurora forecast for upcoming nights. Take a gentle walk along the beachfront to breathe in the crisp Icelandic sea air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to the famous Golden Circle route — begin with Þingvellir National Park (Thingvellir), a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet and where Iceland's first parliament was established in 930 AD. Walk through the dramatic rift valley (free entry to the park, ~750 ISK for parking). Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes, shooting boiling water 20-30 meters into the air (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Complete the Golden Circle with a visit to Gullfoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's most powerful and beautiful waterfalls, particularly dramatic in winter with ice formations (free entry). Drive back to the resort. Dinner at the resort or nearby restaurant. Check aurora forecast for a potential late-night viewing from the resort beach.

meals.breakfast: Late resort breakfast buffet.
meals.lunch: Geysir Center restaurant or café — lamb soup and bread is a warming classic (~2,500-3,500 ISK). Alternatively, pack sandwiches from the resort.
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant dinner — try Icelandic lamb stew or fresh fish of the day. Budget ~4,000-6,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle loop is approximately 300 km and takes a full day. Roads in January can be icy — drive carefully and check road conditions at road.is before departing. Wear crampons/ice cleats at Þingvellir and Gullfoss as paths can be very slippery. Sunset is around 16:30 so Gullfoss may be visited in near-darkness — bring a headlamp.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating back to 1891, set in a natural hot spring surrounded by geothermal activity and small geysers. The Secret Lagoon is far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and offers a more authentic, rustic experience (~3,000 ISK entry). The pool maintains a comfortable 38-40°C temperature year-round. Soak for 1.5-2 hours enjoying the steam and surrounding winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey from Flúðir, stop at Kerið Volcanic Crater — a stunning red and black volcanic crater lake (~400 ISK entry). Walk the rim of the crater and down to the vivid teal-colored lake. Continue back toward the resort area and stop at the town of Selfoss for a coffee break and a browse of local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing evening. Take advantage of any hot tub or geothermal pool facilities at Aegean Bliss Resort. Keep watch for the northern lights from the beachfront — the resort's location away from major city light pollution can make for excellent viewing on clear nights.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast to get an early start for the drive to Flúðir (~1.5 hours from the Keflavik area).
meals.lunch: Café at the Secret Lagoon or a packed lunch — the café offers light snacks and hot drinks. Alternatively, stop in Selfoss at Kaffi Krús for homemade soup and bread (~2,000-3,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using Icelandic ingredients from a local grocery store (Netto or Bónus) to save budget — fresh Icelandic salmon with potatoes and vegetables is delicious and affordable (~2,000-3,000 ISK for ingredients). Or dine at the resort restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is approximately 100 km from Reykjavik and 1.5 hours from the Keflavik area. Book tickets online in advance. The surrounding mini-geysers erupt periodically — a fascinating natural spectacle. Towel rental is available. The drive through the Icelandic countryside in winter is beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: South Coast adventure — drive east along Iceland's stunning South Coast. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — a magnificent 60-meter waterfall that you can walk behind on a path (be aware the path behind may be icy/closed in January — check locally). The waterfall is illuminated at night and magical in winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Skógafoss Waterfall — another iconic 60-meter waterfall with a wide curtain of water. Climb the staircase to the right of the falls for panoramic views over the South Coast (free entry). Continue to the black sand beach of Reynisfjara — one of the world's most dramatic beaches with towering basalt column formations (Reynisdrangar sea stacks) and powerful Atlantic waves. Exercise extreme caution with sneaker waves — never turn your back on the ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the nearby village of Vík í Mýrdal — Iceland's southernmost village with the iconic black-sand beach and dramatic cliff scenery. Explore briefly before driving back toward the resort (approximately 2.5-3 hours). Check aurora forecast — the South Coast offers dark skies excellent for northern lights viewing on the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — pack snacks for the road.
meals.lunch: Black Beach Restaurant in Vík or Suður-Vík Restaurant — fish soup or lamb burger in a cozy setting overlooking the black sand beach (~3,000-4,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Early dinner in Vík before the return drive, or pack food and stop at a scenic pullout on the way back. Alternatively, late dinner at the resort upon return.

day_by_day.notes: The full South Coast day trip is approximately 500 km round trip from the Keflavik area — a long but spectacular drive. Start early (by 08:30) to maximize the limited daylight hours (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~16:30). Check road.is for conditions. The South Coast road (Route 1) is generally well-maintained but can have ice patches in January.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day at the resort — recover from the South Coast adventure. Enjoy a slow breakfast, use resort amenities, and plan the second half of the trip. If the resort has a geothermal pool or hot tub, spend time relaxing in it. Alternatively, visit a local Icelandic community swimming pool (sundlaug) — every Icelandic town has one with hot pots, steam rooms, and lap pools at very affordable prices (~1,000-1,200 ISK entry). The Reykjanesbær Swimming Pool is nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula's geothermal and volcanic landscape further. Visit the Seltún Geothermal Area in Krýsuvík — colorful boiling mud pools, fumaroles, and steaming vents in a surreal landscape (free entry). The rainbow-colored ground of sulfur yellows, reds, and oranges is otherworldly. Nearby, Lake Kleifarvatn — Iceland's largest lake on the Reykjanes Peninsula — offers dramatic winter scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a relaxed evening. Enjoy dinner at the resort restaurant. Tonight, make a dedicated effort to watch for the northern lights from the beachfront — set an alarm for midnight and 2 AM to check conditions if the forecast is favorable.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — leisurely morning.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or a nearby café — Icelandic fish soup or a skyr parfait with granola.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner at the resort restaurant — try the Icelandic lamb rack or fresh Atlantic cod. Budget ~5,000-7,500 ISK per person with a glass of local craft beer.

day_by_day.notes: January 22 is roughly the midpoint of the trip — a good day to rest, do laundry, and recharge. The Seltún area has excellent boardwalks but can be icy — wear crampons. Do not step off marked paths as the ground can be dangerously thin over boiling water. Krýsuvík church nearby is a charming historical stop.

day_by_day.morning: Second Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — book a second aurora tour for tonight (see evening). Use the morning to visit the Reykjavik Art Museum (Listasafn Reykjavíkur) — three venues showcasing Icelandic and international modern art (~2,200 ISK). Alternatively, visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an archaeological museum built around the remains of a Viking-age longhouse from 871 AD (~2,200 ISK). Both are excellent rainy/snowy day options.
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse the Kolaportið Flea Market in Reykjavik (open weekends 11:00-17:00, free entry) — a beloved local institution selling vintage clothing, Icelandic books, second-hand items, and traditional Icelandic foods including hákarl and dried fish. Pick up unique souvenirs at local prices. Visit Harpa Concert Hall — Reykjavik's stunning glass and steel concert hall on the harbor waterfront (free to enter the lobby and admire the architecture).
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Super Jeep tour — second attempt for optimal aurora viewing. Having two separate nights booked increases the probability of clear skies significantly in January. The guides will chase the clearest skies in Iceland, potentially driving 1-2 hours from the city.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or stop at a Reykjavik café — try Brauð & Co bakery for exceptional sourdough bread and pastries (~1,500-2,000 ISK).
meals.lunch: Kolaportið Flea Market food stalls — try traditional Icelandic snacks including dried fish (harðfiskur) with butter, a classic Icelandic snack (~500-1,000 ISK). Or grab a hot dog from a nearby Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur stand — the most famous hot dog stand in Iceland.
meals.dinner: Early dinner before the aurora tour — Snaps Bistro Bar in Reykjavik for French-Icelandic fusion or Grillmarkaðurinn (Grill Market) for Icelandic fine casual dining (~5,000-7,000 ISK per person).

day_by_day.notes: Booking two separate Northern Lights tours on different nights is highly recommended for January travel — cloud cover is unpredictable and having two attempts significantly improves your chances. Most companies allow rebooking if cancelled. The Kolaportið Flea Market is only open on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Snæfellsnes Peninsula day trip — depart early for the magical Snæfellsnes Peninsula, home to the iconic Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano (immortalized in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth'). Drive north along Route 1 and then west on Route 54. First stop: Kirkjufell Mountain and Kirkjufellsfoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's most photographed landscapes, particularly magical in winter with possible snow and ice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around the Snæfellsnes Peninsula. Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach with dramatic sea stacks and lava formations. Stop at Arnarstapi fishing village with its dramatic basalt arch formations and birdlife. If weather permits, drive toward Snæfellsjökull National Park visitor center for views of the glacier (the summit road is closed in winter). The peninsula offers incredible volcanic and coastal scenery throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to the resort (approximately 2.5 hours from the tip of the peninsula). The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is known as a prime northern lights viewing location — if the forecast is good, pull over on the dark peninsula road for aurora viewing before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Very early resort breakfast — pack a thermos of coffee and snacks for the road.
meals.lunch: Fjöruhúsið Café in Hellnar — a charming seaside café serving excellent fish soup, lamb soup, and waffles with cream in a cozy historic setting (~2,500-3,500 ISK). One of Iceland's most beloved hidden cafés.
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the resort upon return, or stop in Borgarnes on the return journey at Settlement Center Restaurant for a hearty Icelandic dinner (~4,000-6,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes Peninsula is approximately 2.5-3 hours from the Keflavik area — a very long day trip. Depart by 07:30-08:00 to maximize daylight. The peninsula is nicknamed 'Iceland in Miniature' for its diversity of landscapes. Roads can be challenging in January — check road.is and consider if a guided tour would be preferable for this day.

day_by_day.morning: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs — note that the Landmannalaugar Highlands are inaccessible by normal vehicles in January due to deep snow and closed mountain roads. However, specialized super jeep tours operate year-round to this incredible destination. Book a guided Landmannalaugar super jeep tour departing from Reykjavik. The tour traverses snow-covered lava fields and rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains to reach the natural geothermal hot spring pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Landmannalaugar (approximately 3-4 hours by super jeep in winter conditions). Soak in the natural hot spring — a surreal experience surrounded by snow-capped multicolored mountains. The contrast of the warm geothermal water against the winter landscape is extraordinary. Explore the immediate area on foot if weather permits. The rhyolite mountains display incredible shades of red, orange, yellow, green, and purple even in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to Reykjavik/resort area (3-4 hours). This is a full-day expedition. Arrive back at the resort by 20:00-21:00. Enjoy a well-deserved hot shower and a relaxing dinner. Check aurora forecast for a potential late-night viewing from the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the tour operator or bring your own thermos of soup and sandwiches — there are no restaurants at Landmannalaugar in winter.
meals.dinner: Comfort dinner at the resort restaurant — treat yourself after the adventurous day. Try the Icelandic meat soup or a hearty lamb dish (~4,000-6,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The Landmannalaugar winter super jeep tour is one of Iceland's most exclusive and spectacular experiences. Book well in advance — tours are limited in winter. Cost is higher than standard tours (~25,000-35,000 ISK per person) but represents incredible value for the experience. Bring a swimsuit, towel, and multiple warm layers. The hot spring has no changing facilities in winter — change quickly in the cold.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed final full morning at the resort. Enjoy a long breakfast, pack any souvenirs carefully, and take a final walk along the Icelandic beachfront. Visit the local geothermal swimming pool one last time for a relaxing soak — a perfect way to reflect on the journey. Browse any local shops for last-minute Icelandic gifts: skyr, Icelandic salt, lopapeysa wool products, or lava soap.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for a final afternoon of exploration. Visit any sites missed earlier in the trip — the Perlan Museum (Wonders of Iceland exhibition with a real indoor ice cave, ~3,900 ISK) offers excellent aurora and glacier exhibits. Alternatively, take a whale watching tour from the Old Harbour (winter tours run year-round, ~10,000-12,000 ISK — humpback whales are often spotted year-round in Faxaflói Bay).
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Reykjavik — celebrate the end of an incredible Icelandic adventure with a special meal. After dinner, one final aurora check — walk to a dark area near the resort beach for a last attempt at northern lights viewing. Pack bags and prepare for early departure.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — savor the last Icelandic breakfast spread.
meals.lunch: Reykjavik street food — visit Hlemmur Mathöll food hall in central Reykjavik for an eclectic mix of Icelandic and international street food vendors (~2,000-3,500 ISK). An excellent spot to try multiple Icelandic flavors in one place.
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market Restaurant) — elegant Icelandic-Asian fusion seafood in Reykjavik (~7,000-10,000 ISK per person). Splurge-worthy for the final night. Alternatively, Grillmarkaðurinn for premium Icelandic ingredients at mid-to-upper range pricing.

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time for Day 13 and plan accordingly. If the flight is early morning, consider an earlier bedtime. Settle the resort bill and confirm any outstanding bookings or returns (rental car, etc.). January 26 may offer one final excellent aurora opportunity — keep the forecast app open all evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Wake up for a last sunrise (around 11:00 in late January — Iceland's winter sunrises are breathtakingly beautiful with long golden-hour light). Enjoy final resort breakfast. Complete packing, check out of Aegean Bliss Resort, and load the vehicle. If time permits before departure, make one final stop at the Blue Lagoon — they offer early morning entry slots starting from 08:00, and the lagoon is magical in the pre-dawn darkness with steam rising into the cold air. The Blue Lagoon is conveniently located just minutes from Keflavik Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Keflavik International Airport — allow at least 2-3 hours before your flight for check-in, security, and any duty-free shopping. Keflavik Airport has good duty-free shops for Icelandic spirits (Brennivín), chocolate, and souvenirs at competitive prices. Board your return flight carrying memories of geothermal hot springs, dramatic volcanic landscapes, and (hopefully) the dancing northern lights.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — farewell to Iceland. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in the Land of Fire and Ice.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or Blue Lagoon café for a pre-departure treat.
meals.lunch: Keflavik Airport restaurants — Pylsuvagninn for a final Icelandic hot dog, or Islenski Barinn for a sit-down Icelandic meal before departure (~3,000-5,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Return the rental car with a full tank of petrol — fuel stations are available near the airport. Keflavik Airport has a luggage storage facility if needed. Allow extra time for check-in in January as weather delays can affect schedules. Duty-free alcohol in Iceland is significantly cheaper than in stores — purchase limits apply per traveler. Keep a small amount of ISK for any final purchases as some small vendors may not accept foreign cards.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover to maximize your viewing experience, often venturing to remote lava fields or frozen lakes for a dramatic backdrop.
experiences.location: Þingvellir National Park, Golden Circle region

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. The average water temperature of 39°C (102°F) is perfect for relaxing while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Includes access to steam rooms, saunas, and the famous silica mud mask stations. Book well in advance as slots fill up fast.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geothermal activity, bubbling hot springs, and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this offers an authentic and intimate geothermal bathing experience in a stunning rural setting.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its culinary scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional dishes like skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, the colorful old harbor, and learn about Norse mythology and the settlement history at the Settlement Exhibition.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's otherworldly rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands to reach the legendary natural geothermal hot spring pool at Landmannalaugar. The hike winds through obsidian lava fields, steaming fumaroles, and vibrant multi-colored hills before rewarding you with a warm soak in the natural pool. A truly bucket-list Icelandic experience combining hiking and hot springs.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a welcome drink at the hotel bar, and settle into your beachfront suite. Light late-night room service recommended.

meals.breakfast: On board or at airport
meals.lunch: On board or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — request the chef's premium charcuterie board and Icelandic smoked salmon platter with a glass of Champagne

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Request early check-in amenities such as warm towels, herbal tea, and a turn-down service. Keep Day 1 light to recover from jet lag.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a gourmet breakfast at the resort. Take a slow walk along the beachfront to acclimate to Iceland's dramatic winter landscape and crisp Arctic air. Explore the resort's premium spa facilities and heated indoor pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — soak in the milky-blue, mineral-rich geothermal waters averaging 38–40°C. Book the premium 'Retreat' package which includes a private changing suite, silica mud mask, algae mask, and access to the exclusive in-water bar serving sparkling wine.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Dinner at a top Reykjavík restaurant such as Dill (Iceland's only Michelin-starred restaurant) — experience New Nordic cuisine with locally foraged ingredients and an exceptional wine pairing menu.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — Icelandic skyr parfait, smoked lamb, fresh pastries, and Valhalla coffee
meals.lunch: In-water floating tray dining at the Blue Lagoon — smoked salmon bites, Icelandic rye bread, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavík — tasting menu with wine pairing (~ISK 25,000–35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Blue Lagoon Retreat package well in advance as slots fill quickly. Transfer from resort to Blue Lagoon takes approximately 20–30 minutes by private car.

day_by_day.morning: Join a Reykjavík Food & Culture Walking Tour — explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its culinary scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr, lamb soup, and fresh langoustine. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and Harpa Concert Hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Museum of Iceland and the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) to immerse in Viking-age history. Browse the luxury boutiques along Laugavegur street for premium Icelandic wool designs and local artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — depart at dusk with an expert guide into the Icelandic wilderness, far from city light pollution, for the best chance of witnessing the Aurora Borealis. The super jeep navigates Iceland's rugged terrain to find optimal viewing conditions.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Tasting stops included in the Food & Culture Walking Tour — supplement with a sit-down lunch at Messinn Restaurant (renowned for their Icelandic fish pan dishes)
meals.dinner: Late dinner after the Northern Lights tour at Grillið Restaurant atop the Radisson Blu Saga Hotel — panoramic Reykjavík views and premium Icelandic lamb and seafood

day_by_day.notes: Northern Lights sightings depend on solar activity (Kp index) and clear skies. January offers long dark nights, maximizing aurora chances. Tour operators monitor forecasts and will select the best location on the night.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided Golden Circle tour — visit Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site, where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet), the erupting Strokkur Geyser at Geysir Geothermal Area, and the majestic Gullfoss waterfall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle with a stop at Kerið volcanic crater lake. Descend into the vibrant red and green caldera for a surreal winter landscape experience. Enjoy hot cocoa and Icelandic waffles at a nearby farmhouse café.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a private in-suite couples' spa treatment at Aegean Bliss Resort followed by a candlelit dinner at the resort's signature restaurant featuring seasonal Icelandic ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic hamper prepared by the resort chef — smoked lamb sandwiches, Skyr dip with rye crackers, thermos of Icelandic lamb soup, and hot coffee
meals.dinner: Signature restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort — premium tasting menu featuring Arctic char, reindeer tenderloin, and Icelandic cheese board with local honey

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver-guide for the Golden Circle for maximum flexibility and comfort. The Golden Circle loop is approximately 300 km and takes 6–8 hours. Dress in thermal layers — January temperatures can reach -10°C.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating to 1891. Soak in the natural hot spring pool surrounded by steaming geothermal vents and a small geyser. The intimate, rustic setting offers a more authentic and less crowded alternative to the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Haukadalur geothermal valley nearby — walk among bubbling mud pools, steaming fumaroles, and vibrant mineral-stained terrain. Visit a local Icelandic horse farm for a private interaction and optional short ride on these famous small, hardy horses.
day_by_day.evening: Second Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — a second attempt maximizes aurora viewing chances during your stay. January's extended darkness (only 4–5 hours of daylight) provides an excellent aurora window.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Matur og Drykkur in Reykjavík (if routing back through the city) — traditional Icelandic recipes reimagined with modern technique; try the salted cod's head and Icelandic lamb neck
meals.dinner: Post-aurora late dinner at Apotek Restaurant, Reykjavík — elegant Nordic-international fusion in a stunning apothecary-themed setting

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is approximately 1.5 hours from Reykjavík. Book tickets in advance. Water temperature is maintained at around 38–40°C year-round. Bring a swimsuit and towel (rentals available on-site).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort. Enjoy a private yoga or meditation session arranged by the resort on the beachfront (weather permitting) or in a heated studio. Indulge in a premium spa treatment — hot stone massage or volcanic mud wrap.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private helicopter tour over the Reykjanes Peninsula — soar above volcanic craters, lava fields, steaming fissures, and the dramatic coastline. Land near a remote geothermal hotspot for a champagne toast and exclusive photo opportunity.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert at Harpa Concert Hall in Reykjavík — Iceland Symphony Orchestra performances are world-class. Pre-book premium seats. Enjoy the iconic glass facade illuminated against the winter night sky.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast delivered by butler service — Eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh-pressed juice, and Icelandic pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort's spa lounge — avocado and smoked trout open sandwich, fresh fruit, and herbal infusions
meals.dinner: Óx Restaurant, Reykjavík — exclusive 20-seat chef's counter restaurant (sister to Dill) offering an intimate, theatrical tasting experience with only one seating per evening. Advance reservation essential.

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours are weather-dependent. Have a backup activity (e.g., a private museum tour or cooking class) arranged. Óx Restaurant requires reservations months in advance — book before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the South Coast — private guided tour to Seljalandsfoss waterfall (walk behind the curtain of water, weather permitting) and the hidden Gljúfrabúi canyon waterfall. Continue to the dramatic black sand beach at Reynisfjara with its iconic basalt column formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the glacier town of Vík í Mýrdal and explore the striking Reynisdrangar sea stacks. Continue to Skógafoss waterfall — climb the 527 steps to the viewing platform for panoramic views across the South Coast. Visit the nearby Skógar Folk Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey with a stop at a remote geothermal hot pot — a private, off-the-beaten-path natural pool arranged exclusively by your guide. Soak under the stars with a glass of Icelandic craft beer or warm spiced wine.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Strondin Bistro & Bar in Vík — locally sourced Icelandic lamb burger, fish and chips with Arctic char, and fresh-baked bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Rangá's Aurora Restaurant (if routing via Hella) — one of Iceland's finest dining experiences with panoramic views and a world-class wine cellar; or return to resort for a private chef dinner

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast tour is approximately 300–400 km round trip. January daylight is limited (approx. 5 hours), so maximize the brief afternoon light for waterfall and beach photography. Waterproof gear is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Private glacier hiking experience on Sólheimajökull glacier — guided walk across the ancient ice with crampons and ice axes provided. Explore ice caves, crevasses, and stunning blue ice formations. This is one of Iceland's most accessible glacier tongues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Jökulsárlón glacier lagoon — witness enormous blue icebergs calving from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier and drifting across the lagoon. Walk to Diamond Beach where translucent icebergs wash ashore on black volcanic sand, creating a magical contrast.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight stay at a luxury property near the glacier lagoon (e.g., Fosshotel Glacier Lagoon or Hali Country Hotel) — or return to Aegean Bliss Resort by private transfer. If staying locally, enjoy a private northern lights viewing from the hotel's outdoor terrace.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure
meals.lunch: Packed luxury lunch hamper — Icelandic lamb pâté, sourdough bread, aged Gouda, dried fruits, and a thermos of hot soup
meals.dinner: Dinner at Fosshotel Glacier Lagoon restaurant (if staying overnight) — locally inspired Nordic menu with glacier views; or private chef experience back at Aegean Bliss Resort

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 4.5 hours from Reykjavík. An overnight stay in the area is highly recommended to allow more time at the lagoon and Diamond Beach at different light conditions. Pre-book glacier hiking guide.

day_by_day.morning: If stayed overnight near Jökulsárlón: Early morning return to Diamond Beach to catch the ethereal blue hour light on the icebergs. Visit Fjallsárlón glacier lagoon (smaller and less crowded than Jökulsárlón) for a serene, intimate glacier experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return journey westward along the South Coast Ring Road — stop at the Fjaðrárgljúfur canyon (a breathtaking 2 km long, 100 m deep canyon) and the Kirkjugólf basalt floor formation near Kirkjubæjarklaustur.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a full resort evening — private hot tub session on the beachfront suite terrace, in-room butler service with a curated cheese and charcuterie board, and a premium whisky or Cognac nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the overnight hotel or a local café near Jökulsárlón
meals.lunch: Lunch at Systrakaffi in Kirkjubæjarklaustur — cozy café with homemade Icelandic soups, lamb stew, and freshly baked cinnamon rolls
meals.dinner: In-suite private dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — request a customized menu from the executive chef featuring the day's freshest Icelandic seafood

day_by_day.notes: The return journey from Jökulsárlón to the resort is approximately 4–5 hours. Depart by midday to ensure safe arrival before full darkness. Roads can be icy — private driver essential.

day_by_day.morning: Full resort wellness morning — begin with a sunrise meditation session (or blue hour, given January's late sunrise), followed by a 90-minute premium couple's spa ritual at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the resort's thermal pools, steam room, and sauna.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided Snæfellsnes Peninsula day tour — visit the mystical Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano (inspiration for Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth'), Arnarstapi fishing village, Lóndrangar basalt pillars, and Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — third dedicated aurora hunt. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula's remote location offers excellent dark sky conditions. Your guide will position the group at the optimal location based on real-time aurora forecasts.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely in-suite breakfast — smoked salmon eggs royale, fresh Icelandic pastries, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Narfeyrarstofa Restaurant in Stykkishólmur — elegant harbour-side dining with fresh Icelandic scallops, langoustine bisque, and pan-fried Arctic char
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the resort after the aurora hunt — warm Icelandic lamb stew, freshly baked rye bread, and a glass of robust red wine

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes Peninsula is approximately 2–2.5 hours from Reykjavík. The peninsula is often called 'Iceland in miniature' due to its diverse landscapes. January weather can be unpredictable — flexible scheduling is advised.

day_by_day.morning: Private Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs experience — trek through Iceland's otherworldly rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains (accessible in winter by super jeep) to reach the legendary geothermal hot springs. Soak in the naturally heated pools surrounded by snow-dusted obsidian lava fields and steaming fumaroles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Landmannalaugar area — visit the Ljótipollur crater lake (one of Iceland's most colorful volcanic craters) and walk along steaming geothermal vents. The contrasting colors of the rhyolite mountains against winter snow create an extraordinary photographic landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by private super jeep. Enjoy a celebratory dinner at the resort's finest restaurant or a top Reykjavík establishment, reflecting on the week's adventures.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure
meals.lunch: Luxury thermos and hamper lunch in the Highlands — hot lamb soup, smoked reindeer, Icelandic rye flatbread, and hot chocolate with Icelandic schnapps
meals.dinner: Dinner at Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market Restaurant), Reykjavík — Iceland's premier Japanese-Icelandic fusion seafood restaurant with an exceptional sake and wine list

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar is only accessible in winter via specialized super jeeps with experienced highland guides. The route involves river crossings and rugged F-roads. Book a reputable highland tour operator. Water temperature in the hot spring is approximately 39–40°C.

day_by_day.morning: Private whale watching tour from Reykjavík Old Harbour — winter whale watching offers sightings of humpback whales, minke whales, and harbor porpoises. Board a premium small-group boat with heated cabins, binoculars, and expert marine biologist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjavík Art Museum and the Einar Jónsson Museum & Sculpture Garden. Visit the Perlan Museum — a stunning glass dome building featuring interactive exhibitions on Iceland's natural wonders, a real indoor ice cave, and a 360° observation deck with panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell luxury dinner at a top Reykjavík restaurant — Geysir Restaurant or Kolabrautin atop the Harpa Concert Hall, offering stunning panoramic views of the city, harbor, and mountains. Splurge on the full tasting menu with Icelandic wine and spirits pairing.

meals.breakfast: Final resort gourmet breakfast — request a special spread from the chef
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic comfort food: plokkfiskur (fish stew), rye bread ice cream, and Icelandic meat soup
meals.dinner: Kolabrautin Restaurant at Harpa Concert Hall — premium tasting menu with panoramic harbor views; signature dishes include Icelandic langoustine, lamb loin, and skyr cheesecake with crowberry compote

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching is weather and sea-condition dependent. Dress in multiple warm layers — the ocean is significantly colder than on land. Tour operators provide thermal overalls. Kolabrautin reservation essential — book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy a leisurely checkout breakfast and last soak in the resort's thermal facilities. Pack and prepare for departure. Request a late checkout if the flight schedule allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Blue Lagoon visit (if time permits before departure) — book the premium Retreat Spa package for a luxurious send-off. The Blue Lagoon is conveniently located between Reykjavík and Keflavík International Airport, making it a perfect final stop. Alternatively, browse last-minute luxury souvenirs at the Keflavík airport duty-free shops.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport. Depart Iceland with extraordinary memories of aurora hunts, geothermal soaks, glacier walks, and world-class Nordic dining.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — full Icelandic spread with skyr, smoked fish, lamb, fresh pastries, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Blue Lagoon's LAVA Restaurant (if visiting) — open-faced smoked salmon sandwich and Icelandic vegetable soup
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on-board — request a special meal if flying business or first class

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the resort and ensure private transfer to the airport is booked. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport security and duty-free shopping. Keflavík Airport has a solid selection of premium Icelandic products including Brennivín schnapps, Icelandic wool goods, and luxury skincare from the Blue Lagoon brand.
